decisions.body:
Decision on the task 3.0a escalation: option A, refined.

All five premises you listed are confirmed on the task branch. The root cause is one level up: the `:httpegress` rules (https-only, operator host list, blocked address classes) were designed for a URL the gnome writes (the `http` check's manifest target). The GitHub client's URLs are written by the operator (`tracker.github.api-url`, `factory.check.github-actions`). One allowlist policy was serving two authors, which is why GHES/Gitea on `http://localhost` and the tracker's own API host could never be admitted by the manifest allowlist.

The decision, folded into the change artifacts on this branch (design D16 as amended 2026-11-08; proposal FR15, FR17, NFR-R5, UX4, NG7; new delta `specs/verification/factory-egress-allowlist`; tasks 3.0a/3.0b):

- **Egress admission follows the author of the URL.** A manifest target is admitted by the operator allowlist alone. An operator connection is admitted by its own configured URL (scheme and host) plus the redirect hosts the built-in declares (github.com defaults: `results-receiver.actions.githubusercontent.com`, `*.blob.core.windows.net`; GHES names its store under a `redirect-hosts` connection key). Judged at load; a refusal is a located configuration error.
- **Shared by both authors:** address-class judgement, the hop bound, the cross-host header strip.
- **Per consumer, not per leaf:** body bound, request timeout and the refusal's configuration key are parameters of the consumer's exchange; the job log is read as a bounded tail. `Response` carries the headers.
- **Hop rule by status:** 301/302/303 → GET without body; 307/308 keep method and body.
- **A refusal is a configuration fault:** never retried, never an outage signal, the error names the key. It must not travel as the IOException class the retry wraps.
- The test posture dissolves by construction: a WireMock or Gitea operator URL on `http://localhost` is admitted as declared, so no test-only switch.

What this means for you:

1. **Task 3.0a is narrowed to the package move with unchanged behavior.** Move `adapter.github` into `:githubapi`; the client keeps its own `HttpClient` for this task; retarget the `PENDING` row of `HttpClientConstructionBoundarySpec` to the new path with 3.0b named as the task that deletes it. Everything else in the task text stands. Continue from 3.0a.
2. **New task 3.0b** carries the guard work above (leaf changes, `GithubHttpClient` over the guarded exchange, refusal classification, consumer list, old-way sweep, one feature per ADDED scenario, `EgressAdmissionByAuthorSpec`, glossary and operator guide). Its precondition is `/review-artifacts migrate-verify-to-executor-contract D16` with findings resolved, as the design-decisions rule requires for a decision added mid-implementation. Do not start 3.0b before that review has run.
3. Tasks 3.3 and 3.5 gained the default redirect hosts in describe and the optional `redirect-hosts` key; read them again before taking them.

Pull the branch before resuming: the artifacts changed in `5936abb6`.

decisions.body:
Decision on the escalation of task 3.0a (options A/B/C): none as offered. Your five
premises were verified and stand; the review found the 2026-11-08 amendment itself
unsound and replaced it. Design D16 is restated (commit <hash> on the task branch),
with proposal FR17, NFR-S1, NG7, NG8, the delta `verification/factory-egress-allowlist`
rewritten, three new deltas (`operator/operator-configuration`, `sandbox/sandbox-egress`,
`operator/vendor-connection-profile`), and tasks 3.0a, 3.0b, 3.0c, 3.3, 3.5 revised.

The decision, in short:
- Admission follows the MEDIUM of a URL, not its author's role. A host an operator file
  names (`factory.check.<name>`, `factory.connections.<name>`, the egress block) is granted.
  A host the law tree names (a manifest target, an inline `tracker.github.api-url`, an
  `executors.<name>.egress` entry) is a request, admitted only by an operator grant or by
  the vendor default the describe declares (`api.github.com`); otherwise a located load
  error naming the two ways to grant it. `.gnomish/config.yaml` is the repository's, not
  the operator's — that was the false premise of the first amendment.
- One entry grammar, one owner: `EgressEntries` moves from `sandbox/core` into
  `:httpegress`; `EgressAllowlist` parses through it. Grammar: exact host, `*.suffix`
  (never the apex), IP literal, CIDR, the class words `loopback` and `private`;
  cloud-metadata addresses are liftable by nothing. `host:port` is NG8.
- One operator block `factory.egress` with scopes `sandbox` (sandbox-boundary level) and
  `in-process` (project level). `factory.sandbox.egress-allowlist` and
  `factory.check.http.allowlist` become removed keys naming their replacement. A
  connection or profile may carry its own `egress` list. The `redirect-hosts` key and the
  term "declared redirect hosts" are withdrawn: a redirect target is judged against the
  same admitted set (connection host, connection `egress`, describe `egress`, `in-process`).
- Load resolves no name: scheme, host, grammar, grants and the class of an IP literal are
  judged at load; the address class of every hop at connect; an unresolvable host is an
  infrastructure failure on the transport path, never a configuration refusal.
- Hop rule by status: 301/302/303 → GET without body or `Content-*`; 307/308 keep method
  and body; `https → http` refused; a visited URL is a loop; MAX_REDIRECTS stays 3. A
  cross-host hop drops only the credential deny-set (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, `Host`,
  `Origin`, `Referer`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `WWW-Authenticate`) and keeps every other
  header. "No header at all" is withdrawn.
- Per consumer: the exchange response carries headers; body bound, request timeout and the
  refusal's key are the consumer's. The `http` built-in keeps 1 MiB / 30 s; the GitHub core
  declares 16 MiB / 60 s and reads a job log as a bounded tail. A refusal is classified
  apart from transport: no retry, no outage signal. The tracker declares no `egress`.
- Test posture: the fixtures' operator file grants `loopback` under
  `factory.egress.in-process`; no switch in production code.

Resume at 3.0a as narrowed (the package move with unchanged behaviour; the PENDING row
retargeted, now deleted by 3.0c). Tasks 3.0b and 3.0c carry the precondition
`/review-artifacts migrate-verify-to-executor-contract D16` before they start; run it and
resolve its findings first. Do not re-touch `add-stage-finished-event`; its D7 is fixed by
that change.

lastEscalation.question:
migrate-verify-to-executor-contract: two artifact questions block progress. Neither can be resolved without editing the change's design/specs, which the implement stage may not do.

(1) Task 3.0a is implemented in the working tree (new module :githubapi, 8 classes and 6 specs moved by git mv, behavior unchanged, PENDING row retargeted to 3.0b; :githubapi:test 48/48, :adapters:github:test 694/694, PIT githubapi.* 40/40, M6 grep one hit). It is left unticked because one main-spec scenario contradicts D15: openspec/specs/build-system/module-layering/spec.md:102-116, requirement 'Vertical adapter modules per technology', scenario 'The github vendor bundle is one module', says the shared GitHub HTTP core is 'an internal package of :adapters:github, not a module other adapters can depend on'. The change has no specs/build-system delta, so bootstrap ModuleTreeSpec.groovy:62-82 (the scenario's test) now fails: no production sources remain under adapter/github/. The same spec's 'Layered Gradle module tree' requirement (:9-27) also lists neither :httpegress nor :githubapi. Proposed fix: a MODIFIED delta in this change (scenario title kept): the core is the first-party library :githubapi; the bundle is still one module and only :bootstrap declares it on a production classpath. Then the next round rewrites the ModuleTreeSpec feature to match.

(2) The precondition of task 3.0b, '/review-artifacts migrate-verify-to-executor-contract D16', has run (read-only). Report: temporary-docs/gnomish/github-oinsio-gnomish-factory-121/review-artifacts-d16.md. Verdict: needs revision. CRITICAL: (a) the address-class judgement shared by both admission sources blocks loopback and RFC1918 (BlockedAddressClass.java:38-52; only a literal address in factory.check.http.allowlist is exempt, EgressAllowlist.java:102-109), so an operator connection to gitea.internal or http://localhost (design.md:313, :363-366, the D9 identity spec at :276, the GHES and plain-http scenarios of the factory-egress-allowlist delta :15-25) would be refused; D16 contradicts itself. (b) the module-layering gap from (1). (c) the hop rule '301/302/303 -> GET without body' (delta :55-65) is wider than RFC 9110, JDK Redirect.NORMAL and today's hopTo; the tracker sends DELETE and PATCH (GithubClaimLease.java:207, GithubLabelOps.java:79, GithubHeartbeat.java:132), so a 301 would turn a tracker write into a GET that returns 2xx and is taken as success, a silent lost write. WARNING: request timeout does not bound the body read on JDK 25.0.3 (measured on macOS; JDK 27 does), so the risk row design.md:473-474 is false; the tracker port's exception type for a refusal is not named, and the remote-outage gate in NFR-R5 only takes git signals; judging the connection at load needs DNS (offline commands, unresolvable host unspecified); the D9 row has no type separating the two URL authors and misses the load-time validators (GithubTrackerSubsectionValidator.java:38 and others); D16 does not cite the GitHub-core signatures it changes (GithubHttpClient.send returns HttpResponse<String>, 14 consumers); conflict with add-stage-finished-event's https-only webhook rule; tasks 3.0b and 3.3 both claim the github-actions redirect-host scenarios. Plus 4 text-only suggestions. 3.0b is not started.

What would you have the next round do?
